newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica forest parastatal sale talks resume - paper.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica forest parastatal sale talks resume - paper.

text.p: Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal has allowed talks on the possible sale of state-owned South African Forestry Co (Safcol) to continue, and restructuring options are again being investigated with a decision likely next year, Business Day said on Thursday.
The paper quoted public enterprises office head Sipho Shabalal as saying that Asmal had lifted the supension and allowed the transformation and restructuring committee to continue with its work.

Asmal earlier halted moves to restructure Safcol, saying it was necessary to first establish how the former homeland forests, which government holds as a separate asset to the timber company, would be dealt with.
The possible sale of Safcol is part of a privatisation programme embarked on by the South African government late last year.
Safcol said last month the uncertainty surrounding government's plans for the company would seriously cut into profits in the 1996/97 year.
In the 12 months to June Safcol's earnings slid to 4.3 cents a share from 7.3 cents last year.
